articles.title: Subtraction iodine maps combined with deep learning reconstruction for improved evaluation of bony invasion in temporal bone lesions.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To assess the capability of subtraction iodine maps (SIM) combined with deep learning reconstruction (DLR) to evaluate the identification of bone involvement in patients with temporal bone lesions, compared with conventional enhanced CT with hybrid iterative reconstruction (HIR). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective study continuously recruited seventy-seven patients (mean age: 46.1 ± 18.9 years; 35 males) with temporal bone lesions who underwent enhanced temporal bone CT scans. Pre-contrast and contrast-enhanced phase images were reconstructed using HIR and DLR. The colored SIM fusion images for evaluation were generated by subtracting the pre-contrast image from the contrast-enhanced image to obtain the SIM, which was then overlaid onto the bone window image. Qualitative scores and quantitative parameters were computed and compared among four groups of images: Enhanced-HIR, Enhanced-DLR, SIM-HIR, and SIM-DLR. RESULTS: Quantitative analysis demonstrated that SIM-DLR significantly reduced noise (lower SD values) and increased CNR of the lesion compared to Enhanced-HIR (both p < 0.001). Qualitatively, SIM-DLR exhibited significantly higher scores than conventional Enhanced-HIR in overall image quality, temporal bone lesion detection confidence, lesion contour delineation capability, and temporal bone involvement visualization (all p < 0.001), with high inter-reader agreement (kappa: 0.812-0.904). Enhancement-dependent analysis revealed that SIM showed markedly beneficial scores of lesion detection, contour delineation, and bone involvement visualization in high-enhancement lesions, compared to low-enhancement lesions (all p < 0.05). CONCLUSION: Compared to conventional Enhanced-HIR, SIM-DLR significantly enhanced temporal bone CT imaging by improving image quality, anatomical delineation, and bone involvement visualization, especially for hypervascular lesions. KEY POINTS: Question Accurately assessing bony invasion by temporal bone lesions is challenging on conventional enhanced CT due to poor lesion-to-bone contrast. Findings SIM combined with DLR improve image quality, lesion delineation, and visualization of bone involvement compared to conventional CT. Clinical relevance This technique enhances preoperative evaluation of temporal bone lesions, particularly hypervascular pathologies, aiding surgical planning and potentially improving treatment precision and outcomes.

articles.title: MRI-derived radiomics for prostate cancer active surveillance: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To systematically review MRI-derived radiomic and artificial intelligence models predicting outcomes in men on or eligible for active surveillance (AS) for prostate cancer, and whether reported endpoints permit quantitative synthesis. METHOD: Following PRISMA 2020, we searched PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Web of Science (2000-September 2026). Two reviewers independently screened, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias (QUADAS-2, PROBAST) and methodological quality (METRICS). Three subgroups were defined: AS selection at diagnosis, baseline detection of clinically significant cancer, and progression during follow-up. Pooling was pre-specified for subgroups with at least four independent cohorts; endpoint equivalence was assessed. RESULTS: Seventeen studies across 12 unique cohorts were included. Seven publications derived from two cohorts; 12 independent cohort-level estimates (n = 2703) remained after overlap resolution. Nine publications (four independent cohorts) addressed progression (AUC 0.70 to 0.95), but progression was defined in five non-equivalent ways, from any grade-group increase to composite core-count criteria, precluding quantitative synthesis. Risk of bias was high or unclear in 16 of 17 studies; the median METRICS score was 32.3 % (range 18.9-52.3 %). No study reported external validation or calibration for progression. CONCLUSIONS: Progression endpoints were heterogeneous and several were of limited clinical relevance. A core outcome set for AS (at least ISUP grade group ≥3 and/or unequivocal radiological progression), followed by multi-centre external validation with a head-to-head comparison against the PRECISE v2 (Prostate Cancer Radiological Estimation of Change in Sequential Evaluation) score, is the priority before clinical use can be considered.

articles.title: Abdominal hydatid disease and its mimics: a comprehensive pictorial review of imaging clues to the differential diagnosis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hydatid disease (HD), also known as echinococcosis, is a parasitic disease caused by tapeworms. HD is endemic in many parts of the world and can affect virtually any organ system. Due to the rapid growth of worldwide migration, especially in recent decades, the disease can be diagnosed anywhere, particularly among immigrants in non-endemic areas. OBJECTIVE: To illustrate the spectrum of abdominal imaging manifestations of HD and to review the principal benign and malignant abdominal cystic lesions that can mimic HD, using an organ-based approach with emphasis on imaging features that aid in differential diagnosis. FINDINGS: Radiologic imaging is crucial for diagnosing HD, assessing disease activity, progression, and complications, and detecting stage- and organ-specific features. Hydatid disease in the abdomen can mimic other abdominal diseases, depending on the organ involved. Additionally, many other abdominal lesions can mimic hydatid disease and present with similar clinical symptoms. This pictorial review demonstrates characteristic imaging findings of HD and its mimics across the different abdominal organs and spaces, highlighting specific morphological features and potential diagnostic pitfalls. This review incorporates the World Health Organization Informal Working Group on Echinococcosis (WHO-IWGE) classification to provide a standardized framework for describing the imaging appearances of cystic echinococcosis. CONCLUSION: Recognizing the characteristic imaging features of HD and its mimics is essential for accurate diagnosis and appropriate management. A systematic approach that incorporates lesion morphology, organ involvement, disease stage, and relevant clinical and epidemiological information can improve diagnostic confidence, enable early diagnosis, and help avoid misdiagnosis and inappropriate intervention.

articles.title: CT radiomics and topology-based intratumoral heterogeneity for preoperative prediction of nuclear β-catenin expression in hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Nuclear β-catenin accumulation reflects activation of the Wnt/β-catenin pathway in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but noninvasive preoperative prediction of this immunohistochemical phenotype remains incompletely established. PURPOSE: To develop and externally validate CT radiomics and topology-based intratumoral heterogeneity (ITH) models for preoperative prediction of nuclear β-catenin expression in HCC. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included 1029 patients with histopathologically confirmed HCC. Patients from two participating institutions formed the development cohort and were split into training (n=620; nuclear β-catenin-positive, 293) and internal validation (n=267; nuclear β-catenin-positive, 126) sets. Patients from an independent third institution formed the external validation cohort (n=142; nuclear β-catenin-positive, 43). Whole-tumor portal venous phase CT radiomics features and topology-based ITH features were extracted from the audited image-mask cohort. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were evaluated using AUC, bootstrap 95% confidence intervals, calibration summaries, Brier scores, and decision curve analysis. RESULTS: In external validation, AUCs were 0.677 for the clinical model, 0.862 for the radiomics model, 0.857 for the ITH model, 0.831 for the core ITH model, 0.863 for the radiomics-ITH model, and 0.886 for the stacking model. Compared with radiomics alone, stacking showed a numerical ΔAUC of 0.024 (95% CI, -0.010 to 0.060; P=0.180). CONCLUSION: CT radiomics and topology-based ITH features showed external predictive value for nuclear β-catenin expression in HCC. The stacking model had the highest external AUC, but its improvement over radiomics alone was not statistically significant. If prospectively validated, these CT-based approaches could complement tissue assessment for pretreatment biological stratification.

articles.title: Development and validation of a preoperative CT-based radiomics nomogram for predicting postpancreatectomy acute pancreatitis after pancreatoduodenectomy.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate the value of radiomics based on preoperative contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) for predicting postpancreatectomy acute pancreatitis (PPAP) after pancreatoduodenectomy (PD). METHODS: A retrospective analysis included 104 patients who underwent PD and preoperative CECT between May 2019 and March 2025. Patients were randomly divided into training (n = 73) and test (n = 31) sets at a 7:3 ratio. PPAP was defined according to the biochemical and radiologic components of the International Study Group for Pancreatic Surgery (ISGPS) criteria. After pancreatic parenchyma delineation, radiomics feature extraction and selection, an optimal model was developed on the training set to calculate the radiomics score (rad-score). Independent clinical and morphological features were selected by univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses. Conventional quantitative CT attenuation ratios of the pancreatic parenchyma were also evaluated. Predictive performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. RESULTS: PPAP occurred in 41 patients. Four models were compared: a clinical-morphologic model (age and main pancreatic duct [MPD] dilation), a conventional model (age, MPD dilation and arterial-to-portal ratio [A/P]), a radiomics model (rad-score alone), and a radiomics-integrated model (age, MPD dilation and rad-score). The radiomics-integrated model achieved the highest area under the curve (AUC) among the four models, with the AUC of 0.854 (95% CI 0.758-0.951) in the training set and 0.862 (95% CI 0.732-0.993) in the test set. CONCLUSION: The radiomics-integrated model demonstrated promising performance for preoperative prediction of PPAP after PD, which may facilitate individualized risk stratification and perioperative management.

articles.title: Utility of OpenEvidence and ChatGPT in Selecting Neuroimaging Based on Appropriateness Criteria.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Large Language models (LLMs) are novel tools with promising applications in imaging selection for clinical scenarios, but information is limited on the accuracy of an LLM trained on a medically specific dataset compared to a generalized dataset. In this analysis, we assessed the accuracy of the imaging recommendations by LLMs ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-5.0, and OpenEvidence for neuroradiology, using the American College of Radiology (ACR) Appropriateness Criteria as the reference standard. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Prompts from the ACR Appropriateness Criteria priority clinical areas within neurology were used to build open-ended (OE) or select-all-that-apply (SATA) questions. Each question was posed three times, and the responses were scored against ACR guidelines. The performance of each LLM on OE and SATA was compared, and then was further analyzed by acuity. Mean accuracy scores were calculated by averaging performance across OE and SATA questions for each model. Analysis of variance was then conducted to assess differences in performance among the models. RESULTS: A total of 78 prompts were assessed in 11 priority clinical areas. These areas included cerebrovascular conditions, neurological pain, and spine pathologies. Amongst SATA, Open Evidence performed the best (79.5%) compared to GPT5 (71.2%) and GPT3.5 (44.4%). For the OE prompts, Open Evidence was more accurate (86.3%) than GPT3.5 (69.2%) but not GPT5 (80.6%). Amongst the models, no differences were found based on acuity. CONCLUSION: Overall, OpenEvidence performed the best for both OE and SATA prompts. ChatGPT-5 performed better than ChatGPT3.5 for SATA prompts. LLM performance was unaffected by the acuity of the case.

articles.title: Regular post-treatment surveillance is associated with improved survival in nasopharyngeal carcinoma: a retrospective study.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Benefit of post-treatment surveillance in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), characterized by high recurrence risk, remains unexplored. We explored whether regular post-treatment surveillance facilitates earlier recurrence detection and improves survival. METHODS AND MATERIALS: We identified 8,798 patients with non-metastatic stage I-IVA NPC at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center. The 1-year landmark analysis was chosen as representative of surveillance patterns, dividing patients into regular and irregular surveillance group based on surveillance intensity. Cox proportional hazards models clarified the association between overall survival (OS) and surveillance intensity, with subgroup analyses stratified by clinical stage and pretreatment Epstein-Barr virus DNA level. Survival impact of surveillance imaging for local, regional, and distant sites were also investigated. RESULTS: Median follow-up was 64.8 months. 1-year landmark analysis comprised 4,078 and 4,720 patients receiving regular (≥ 4 visits in the first year) and irregular surveillance (< 4 visits), respectively. Regular surveillance was linked to shorter median recurrence time (26.1 versus 27.0 months) and improved OS (HR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.74-0.99; P = 0.032) after multivariable adjustment. Notably, patients receiving regular imaging surveillance for distant site had better OS (HR, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.57-0.82; P < 0.001) whereas imaging for local (HR, 1.36; 95% CI, 0.90-2.04; P = 0.140) and regional site (HR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.57-1.27; P = 0.428) did not. Regular surveillance patients with distant metastases exhibited fewer metastatic organs (P < 0.001) and earlier recurrence stages (P < 0.001), translating into prolonged post-recurrence survival (HR, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.58-0.80; P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Regular post-treatment surveillance, particularly distant imaging, could improve NPC survival, highlighting an urgency for evidence-based post-treatment surveillance strategies.

articles.title: Uncertainty-aware auto-segmentation enables adaptive radiotherapy planning of liver metastases.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Despite remarkable auto-segmentation performance and growing clinical adoption, models frequently fail to generalize beyond the training distribution. Therefore, this study aimed to develop and validate an uncertainty-aware segmentation pipeline that yields high delineation accuracy for liver cancer patients and reliably identifies safety-critical segmentation imperfections in radiotherapy. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Datasets of n = 173 patients with 224 liver metastases were divided into training (n = 100), validation (n = 33), and test (n = 40). Each case included annotated T2-weighted magnetic resonance images. An nnU-Net segmented treatment-relevant organs and provided a margin-extended hepatic mask, which served as input to a second-stage SE-ResUNet for lesion delineation. Uncertainty was approximated via checkpoint ensembling under a cyclic learning-rate schedule, yielding entropy-based uncertainty maps and case-wise uncertainty scores. These guided an adaptive post-inference analysis consisting of (i) detection of potentially missed lesions and (ii) identification of problematic contours. Performance was evaluated on 40 patients (n = 52 lesions) using Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), 95%-Hausdorff-Distance (HD95), expected calibration error (ECE), uncertainty coverage, and the correlation between case-wise uncertainty scores and segmentation accuracy. RESULTS: Overall performance across treatment-relevant organs was DSC/HD95 = 0.89/4.8 mm; lesionsegmentation achieved DSC/HD95 = 0.86/4.9 mm. Uncertainty-guided post-processing, triggered in 14/40 cases, recovered 7 initially missed metastases, increasing lesion-level sensitivity from 84.6% (44/52) to 98.1% (51/52). Uncertainty estimates showed good calibration with ECE/uncertainty coverage for organs/lesion of 7.2/93.7% and 7.5/98.3%, and significant correlation between uncertainty/DSC (r = -0.802). CONCLUSION: The proposed pipeline seamlessly integrates accurate organ/lesion segmentation, interpretable uncertainty, and anatomy-guided post-processing to detect safety-critical segmentation failures and enable trustworthy AI auto-segmentation in clinical routine.

articles.title: Evaluating imputation methods for longitudinal clinical trajectories: Toxicities in head and neck cancer treatment.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Longitudinally collected medical data is often afflicted by missingness, making methods mitigating missingness valuable. This study evaluated nine imputation methods for longitudinal data, using toxicity scores measured at multiple timepoints resulting from head and neck cancer treatment with radiotherapy. METHODS AND MATERIALS: For four toxicities (xerostomia, dysphagia, taste alteration, and sticky saliva), toxicity scores at 16 timepoints (1 prior, 7 during, and 8 after treatment) were collected, resulting in 1442 patients with on average ∼11.6 available timepoints. Imputation methods ranged from simple to deep learning-based. Methods were evaluated using a systematic removal strategy enabling comparison of true and imputed values. Patient-level, cohort-level and downstream model evaluation was done, evaluating inclusion criteria for patients, training data requirement and modelling effect respectively. RESULTS: General imputation quality showed minimal differences between methods, except simple methods, which performed worse. For patient-level evaluation, it was found that when patients had <50% of timepoints available, imputation started to worsen. Cohort-level evaluation showed that advanced methods could reach good performances at low patient counts (150 patients) but were more severely affected by low average timepoint availability. Downstream model evaluation showed negligible differences between methods, other than simple methods which resulted in different model coefficients. CONCLUSIONS: It was found that it is best to avoid simple imputation methods. Furthermore, when applying imputation to longitudinal data practitioners should be conscientious about inclusion of certain patients and if their dataset permits the use of more advanced imputation methods.

articles.title: From patient-reported outcome scores to clinical meaning: defining thresholds for clinical importance for the EORTC QLQ-PR25 questionnaire for patients with prostate cancer.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Interpretation of patient-reported outcome scores remains challenging. Thresholds for clinical importance (TCIs) can facilitate score interpretation at the individual-patient level. We aimed to establish TCIs for the EORTC QLQ-PR25 to improve the interpretation of prostate cancer (PCa)-specific patient-reported outcomes in clinical practice and research. METHODS: In this prospective multicentre study, 261 patients with PCa from seven countries completed the EORTC QLQ-PR25 and anchor items assessing limitations in daily life, need for help/care, and worries caused by the respective symptom or problem. Receiver operating characteristic analyses were used to derive TCIs for the QLQ-PR25 scales, using a binary criterion for clinical importance based on the anchor items. Sensitivity analyses explored threshold robustness across patient subgroups. RESULTS: For five of the six QLQ-PR25 scales, ROC analyses showed acceptable to excellent discrimination, with AUC values ranging from 0.74 to 0.90. The corresponding TCIs showed sensitivity values between 0.62 and 0.88 and specificity values between 0.48 and 0.98. No meaningful threshold could be established for sexual activity (AUC = 0.48). CONCLUSIONS: This study provides the first TCIs for a questionnaire assessing health-related quality of life in patients with PCa. These thresholds may improve interpretation of individual patient scores, support symptom screening and clinical decision-making, and facilitate the definition of clinically meaningful outcomes in clinical research.

articles.title: Dose-effect analysis of late dental adverse effects following radiation therapy in survivors of paediatric head and neck rhabdomyosarcoma.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Paediatric head and neck rhabdomyosarcomas (HNRMS) often require radiotherapy, causing dental complications during critical development. Limited literature suggests dose-dependent risks, but clear thresholds for late dental adverse effects are lacking. This study aims to characterize dose effects on developing dentition in paediatric HNRMS patients to identify dose-response relationships informing evidence-based treatment planning. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Orthopantomograms from survivors of HNRMS were evaluated using the validated DENTALE scoring system. Radiation doses from brachytherapy, external beam radiation with protons and photons to deciduous teeth were retrieved from treatment plans and converted to EQD2 (α/β = 3 Gy). Dose-response relationships were modelled per tooth using binary logistic regression in Mplus (COMPLEX option for within-patient dependency; model fit assessed by ROC analysis). RESULTS: Among 34 survivors (median age at diagnosis 5.6 years), 27 (79.4 %) exhibited late dental AE. Of 919 assessable permanent teeth, 242 (26.3 %) showed abnormalities. Increasing radiation dose was consistently associated with higher AE probability. The dose corresponding to 50 % predicted probability of any dental AE was 23 Gy(EQD2). Structure-specific thresholds were higher for crowns (68 Gy) and eruption disturbances (52 Gy(EQD2)), and lower for roots (24 Gy(EQD2)) and crown-root ratio abnormalities (36 Gy(EQD2)). CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates dose-effect relationships for radiation exposure of developing dentition, with clinically relevant structure-specific thresholds. Teeth receiving no radiation still show developmental abnormalities, likely due to chemotherapy. These findings support incorporating dentition as organ at risk and dose constraints into paediatric head-and-neck radiotherapy planning to reduce dental morbidity.

articles.title: Five-Year Survival and Durable Local Control After Image-Guided Thermal Ablation for Stage IA Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate five-year overall survival, cancer-specific survival, local tumor progression-free survival, local recurrence, and durable local control after repeat ablation in patients with Stage IA non-small cell lung cancer treated with image-guided thermal ablation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This HIPAA-compliant, institutional review board-approved retrospective cohort study included 85 patients with Stage IA non-small cell lung cancer treated with image-guided thermal ablation between 2011 and 2018. Patients had a single target tumor: 16 T1a, 45 T1b, and 24 T1c tumors. Outcomes included technical success, five-year overall survival (OS), cancer-specific survival (CSS), local tumor progression-free survival (LTPFS), local recurrence, durable local control (no further local recurrence after repeat ablation during follow-up), and adverse events. Kaplan-Meier analysis estimated survival outcomes. RESULTS: Median follow-up was 55.6 months. Ablation modalities included microwave ablation in 41 patients, cryoablation in 37, and radiofrequency ablation in 7. Technical success was 100%. Grade 2 or higher adverse events within 90 days occurred in 8 patients (9.4%), all pneumothoraces requiring chest tubes. Five-year OS was 68.2%, 77.4%, and 68.2%; CSS was 100%, 87.2%, and 100%; and LTPFS was 100%, 77.8%, and 100% for T1a, T1b, and T1c tumors, respectively. Overall five-year LTPFS was 92.6%. Local recurrence occurred in 8 patients (9.4%). Six underwent repeat ablation without subsequent recurrence, yielding durable local control in 97.6%. CONCLUSION: Image-guided thermal ablation provided favorable five-year survival and high durable local control for Stage IA non-small cell lung cancer, supporting ablation as a repeatable and effective treatment option.

articles.title: Comparison of signal drop on T2-weighted and post-contrast T1-weighted Dixon MRI in spinal bone marrow lesions.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare signal drop percentages between in-phase and out-of-phase images on T2-weighted and post-contrast T1-weighted Dixon MRI in spinal bone marrow lesions and evaluate their diagnostic performance in differentiating benign from malignant lesions. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included patients who underwent post-contrast spine MRI with 3.0 T Dixon sequences between January 2023 and January 2024. Signal drop percentages ([in-phase - out-of-phase] / in-phase) were calculated for T2-weighted Dixon (T2 %drop) and post-contrast T1-weighted Dixon images (GdT1 %drop). T2 %drop and GdT1 %drop were compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver-operating characteristic analysis with area under the curve (AUC) calculation. Optimal cutoff values were determined to achieve 100 % sensitivity for malignancy while maximizing specificity. Specificities were compared using the McNemar test. RESULTS: Among 78 patients (median age, 63.5 years [interquartile range (IQR), 54.3-70.8]; 37 men, 41 women; 41 benign, 34 malignant, and 3 indeterminate lesions), median T2 %drop and GdT1 %drop were 29.2 % (IQR, 20.3-46.0) and 21.4 % (IQR, 15.4-28.6), respectively. GdT1 %drop was significantly lower than T2 %drop (P < 0.001). The AUC of GdT1 %drop (0.84; 95 % confidence interval [CI], 0.73-0.92) was numerically lower than that of T2 %drop (0.91; 95 % CI, 0.81-0.97), although the difference was not significant (P = 0.132). The specificity of GdT1 %drop was significantly lower than that of T2 %drop at the optimal cutoff values of 27.9 % and 29.0 %, respectively (39.0 % [95 % CI, 24.2-55.5] vs. 80.5 % [95 % CI, 65.1-91.2]; P < 0.001). CONCLUSION: GdT1 %drop was significantly lower than T2 %drop with substantially lower specificity, warranting cautious interpretation to avoid misclassification.

articles.title: Multiparametric MRI assessment of renal Masses: Diagnostic performance of the modified clear cell likelihood score and ancillary MRI features.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the diagnostic performance and interreader agreement of the Clear Cell Likelihood Score (ccLS), the modified Clear Cell Likelihood Score (m-ccLS), and ancillary MRI features for differentiating benign from malignant renal masses and clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) from non-ccRCC lesions. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 106 patients with renal masses who underwent multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) between 2018 and 2026. MRI features, including T1 signal intensity (SI) ratio, T2 SI ratio, apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) ratio, and arterial-to-delayed enhancement ratio (ADER), were evaluated. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis in both the overall cohort and the cT1a subgroup. Two radiologists independently assigned ccLS and m-ccLS scores and assessed the presence of a pseudocapsule for interreader agreement analysis. RESULTS: Among 106 renal masses, 73 (68.9 %) were classified as cT1a tumors. For differentiating benign from malignant renal masses, m-ccLS demonstrated higher diagnostic performance than ccLS in both the overall cohort (AUC, 0.770 vs. 0.654) and the cT1a subgroup (AUC, 0.784 vs. 0.689). For differentiating ccRCC from non-ccRCC lesions, ccLS and m-ccLS showed comparable diagnostic performance in both the overall cohort (AUC, 0.884 vs. 0.868) and the cT1a subgroup (AUC, 0.885 vs. 0.876). Among the evaluated ancillary MRI features, the T2 SI ratio was significantly associated with both benign-malignant discrimination and ccRCC identification. Interreader agreement for ccLS, m-ccLS, and pseudocapsule assessment was substantial. CONCLUSION: Incorporation of pseudocapsule assessment into the ccLS improved differentiation between benign and malignant renal masses while maintaining comparable diagnostic performance for identifying ccRCC. T2 SI ratio may provide additional value in MRI-based characterization of renal masses.

articles.title: Utility of PSA density velocity in diagnosing prostate cancer on prostate MR.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To assess if PSA density (PSAD) velocity is a predictor of clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa). METHODS: Patients undergoing prostate MR for suspected csPCa between 2017 and 2023 were included. Of these, patients who underwent two or more MR exams within 0.3 to 2 years to each other and pathological confirmation within 1 year after the last MR were identified. PI-RADS score, patient age, no-prior-PCa cohort or active surveillance (AS), PSA, PSAD, PSA-velocity and PSAD-velocity were assessed if they were predictor of csPCa. For univariate analysis, all variables were assessed using student t or chi-square tests. When variables were considered significant, variables were entered into multivariate logistic regression model. To assess whether PSAD-velocity adds diagnostic value beyond established predictors, we compared a base model (age, PI-RADS score, clinical cohort, and current PSAD) with the same model plus PSAD-velocity, using optimism-corrected AUC from 1,000 bootstrap resamples. RESULTS: 23,244 MRs were performed (17,703 for no-prior-PCa, 5,541 for AS). 1,174 patients (mean age: 65.9 years) met the inclusion criteria, and 550 (46.8%) were diagnosed with csPCa. On univariate analysis, PI-RADS score (p<.0001), age (67.0 vs. 64.9 years, p<.0001), AS status (67% vs. 59%, p = .004), PSA (7.5 vs. 6.6 ng/mL, p<.001), PSAD (p<.0001), and PSAD-velocity (0.023 vs. 0.012 ng/mL/mL/year, p = .005) were associated with csPCa, but PSA-velocity (1.4 vs. 1.2 ng/mL/year, p=.38) was not. On multivariable analysis, PI-RADS score (p<.0001), age (p<.0001), AS status (p = .002), PSA (p<.0001), and PSAD (p<.0001) remained significant predictors, but PSAD-velocity was not (p = .13). Adding PSAD-velocity to the base model produced no significant improvement in optimism-corrected AUC (0.7605 vs. 0.7611; ΔAUC = + 0.0006, 95% CI -0.0002 to +0.0019). CONCLUSIONS: Higher PSAD-velocity was associated with presence of csPCa on univariate analysis but not on multivariate analysis, and on fixed-model analysis did not meaningfully improve diagnostic discrimination beyond established predictors.

articles.title: Xenon-129 ventilation imaging in pediatric bronchiolitis obliterans patient.
Iterative Navigator-Based Retrospective Motion Correction for Multi-Shot Brain MR Elastography and Evaluation of Single-Shot Post-Reconstruction Correction.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Brain MR elastography (MRE) is uniquely sensitive to subject motion, as even small phase deviations can produce large errors in the mechanical properties estimated. Existing motion correction strategies have not been validated for MRE and are often incompatible with complex multi-shot or joint temporal reconstructions. METHODS: We propose COMET (Correction Of Motion in Elastography via Transformation), a framework that estimates rigid-body motion from navigator images and embeds transformation matrices into an iterative reconstruction and displacement-vector reorientation for multi-shot MRE. We additionally validate post-reconstruction correction and displacement-vector reorientation for single-shot MRE. The framework was evaluated on MRE from 9 pairs of EPI single-shot and 9 pairs of spiral multi-shot acquisitions, each containing a with-motion scan and a reference. Additionally, four representative motion patterns with increasing amplitude were simulated to indicate how different motions affect MRE quality and results, and a brain tumor MRE dataset with simulated motion was used to assess clinical effect. RESULTS: Motion correction improved stiffness accuracy across all tested datasets, reducing average stiffness errors by up to 240.86% in multi-shot spiral MRE, and by up to 44.28% in single-shot EPI, across in vivo motion ranging from 4.81 to 67.58 mm translation and 1.85°-23.63° rotation. In a pediatric glioma dataset, simulated motion completely obscured tumor stiffness contrast, while correction restored tumor stiffness visibility. Robustness of estimated stiffness maps depended on motion amplitude, temporal motion patterns, and encoding strategies. CONCLUSION: This approach enables robust motion correction for single- and multi-shot brain MRE, and expands reliable MRE to clinical and challenging populations.

articles.title: Myocardial work in light-chain and transthyretin-related amyloidosis with preserved ejection fraction: a cardiovascular magnetic resonance study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate pressure-volume loop (PV-loop) changes by cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging in cardiac amyloidosis (CA) patients with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), and to assess PV-loop parameters' potential as subtype differential diagnostic markers. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Between May 2017 and September 2023, 100 consecutive confirmed CA patients (14 transthyretin-related [ATTR-CA] and 86 light-chain [AL-CA]) and 40 age- and sex-matched healthy controls (HCs) were prospectively enrolled. PV-loop parameters were derived from CMR cine images and brachial blood pressure. Clinical and CMR parameters were compared between CA patients and HCs, as well as between CA subtypes. The correlations between PV-loop parameters and clinical and imaging parameters were assessed. Furthermore, the differential diagnostic performance of these PV-loop parameters was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC). Bootstrapping was performed 2000 times for internal validation. RESULTS: Compared to HCs, CA patients showed significantly lower stroke work index, potential energy index (PEI), and work efficiency (all p < 0.001). AL-CA patients had higher N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) levels (2358.00 [IQR: 903.25, 5559.00] vs 810.00 [IQR: 269.00, 1136.01] pg/mL, p = 0.002) and lower PEI (0.13 [IQR: 0.07, 0.15] vs 0.15 [IQR: 0.13, 0.19] J/m², p = 0.025) than ATTR-CA patients. NT-proBNP (β = -1.94, OR = 0.14, 95% CI: 0.03-0.64, p = 0.016) and PEI (β = 0.20, OR = 1.23, 95% CI: 1.07-1.44, p = 0.007) were independent predictors for AL-CA vs ATTR-CA differentiation, and combining these two parameters enhanced the diagnostic performance (bootstrapping AUC 0.847). CONCLUSION: By providing pathophysiological insights into the distinctions between AL-CA and ATTR-CA, PV-loop parameters have the potential to serve as a complementary, contrast-free approach for differential diagnosis. KEY POINTS: Question PV-loop changes by CMR in CA patients with preserved LVEF remain unknown. Findings Light-chain CA patients with preserved LVEF had higher NT-proBNP levels and lower PEI than transthyretin-related CA patients. Critical relevance statement The CMR-derived PV-loop parameters revealed pathophysiological differences between the two subtypes of CA, suggesting potential differential diagnostic value.

articles.title: Real-time CT/MR fusion imaging-guided core needle biopsy: enhancing diagnostic precision in head and neck lesions.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To establish an intraoperative CT/MR fusion imaging (FI)-guided core needle biopsy (CNB) approach for head and neck lesions and to evaluate its diagnostic performance in comparison with conventional CT-guided biopsy. MATERIAL AND METHODS: This retrospective study included patients undergoing CT-guided or FI-guided CNB for head and neck lesions between January 2020 and December 2024. Clinical information was collected, including demographics, lesion size, needle insertion depth, number of biopsy cores obtained, and complications. Diagnostic performance was evaluated at both the case-based and core-based levels by comparing biopsy histopathology with the final diagnosis. Subgroup analyses were performed according to lesion size, needle insertion depth, and pathological type. RESULTS: A total of 152 patients with 426 biopsy cores were included, comprising 66 patients (183 cores) in the CT-guided group and 86 patients (243 cores) in the FI-guided group. At the case-based level, FI-guided biopsy demonstrated significantly higher diagnostic accuracy than CT-guided biopsy (98.8% vs 90.9%, p = 0.04), particularly for lesions < 3.7 cm and non-squamous cell carcinoma (non-SCC) lesions. At the core-based level, FI-guided biopsy also achieved higher accuracy (96.3% vs 73.2%, p < 0.001) and sensitivity (93.8% vs 65.0%, p < 0.001), with consistent advantages across all predefined subgroups. No major procedure-related complications were observed. CONCLUSIONS: FI-guided CNB is a safe and feasible technique for head and neck lesions that improves diagnostic accuracy compared with conventional CT guidance. KEY POINTS: Question Can CT/MR FI overcome the limitations of conventional CT guidance for precise targeting and accurate biopsy of anatomically complex head and neck lesions? Findings CT/MR FI-guided biopsy demonstrated higher diagnostic accuracy at both case-based and core-based analyses than conventional CT-guided biopsy for complex head and neck lesions. Critical relevance statement This study provides evidence that CT/MR fusion-guided biopsy improves targeting precision and diagnostic performance compared with conventional CT-guided biopsy, supporting its application for complex head and neck lesions in clinical radiology practice.

articles.title: Age, Body Mass Index, and Lumbar Trabecular Bone Score in Type 2 Diabetes: Gender-specific Associations.
articles.abstract: Trabecular bone score (TBS) provides information on bone microarchitecture beyond bone mineral density (BMD) and may be particularly relevant in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). This exploratory cross-sectional study examined associations of age and body mass index (BMI) with lumbar TBS (L1-L4) and their variation by gender in 240 adults with T2DM. Generalized additive models (GAMs) included overall smooths, gender-specific smooths, and tensor-product surfaces. Between-gender smooth contrasts were evaluated using joint simultaneous 95% confidence bands. Supplementary linear-model comparisons assessed fit and repeated five-fold cross-validated prediction errors. Age (edf = 2.767, p < 0.001) and BMI (edf = 2.166, p = 0.001) were associated with TBS in the overall GAM; these tests assessed association rather than departures from linearity. Males had higher TBS than females in the gender-specific smooth model (β = 0.0846, p < 0.001). Direct contrasts supported differences in centered age smooths at approximately 34.0-45.4 and 67.1-74.9 years, but did not identify differences in BMI smooths supported by the simultaneous bands. Gender-specific smooths improved fit over common smooths (p = 0.00133), whereas the additional improvement from tensor-product surfaces did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.08363). GAMs improved in-sample fit but did not consistently reduce cross-validated prediction errors relative to linear alternatives. These findings suggest gender-related variation in the age-TBS association, while evidence for differences in the BMI-TBS association remains insufficient. Residual confounding and the cross-sectional design warrant cautious interpretation and further validation.

articles.title: A Statistically Validated and Explainable Deep Learning Framework for Oral Cancer Classification.
articles.abstract: Despite numerous deep learning models reporting high accuracy for oral cancer classification, most rely on a single train/test split on a single dataset, with limited statistical validation, external generalization testing, or explainability. This study addresses that gap through a statistically validated, externally tested, and dual-explainable classification framework. We provide a rigorous benchmarking study contrasting 20 hybrid combinations (4 pre-trained backbones × 5 classical classifiers) against fine-tuned end-to-end CNNs. Across repeated stratified fivefold cross-validation with 10 repetitions, the hybrid framework consistently outperformed end-to-end CNNs, with ResNet50 paired with an SVM-RBF classifier achieving top performance: 0.960 accuracy (95% CI 0.958-0.963), 0.953 F1-score (95% CI 0.951-0.956), and 0.991 ROC-AUC (95% CI 0.990-0.993), with Wilcoxon signed-rank tests confirming statistical significance (p < 0.001). MobileNetV2 paired with SVM-RBF emerged as an efficient lightweight alternative, suited to resource-constrained point-of-care settings. On an independent external validation dataset, the optimal ResNet50 + SVM-RBF model demonstrated robust generalization, achieving 0.916 accuracy (95% CI 0.892-0.939), 0.984 ROC-AUC (95% CI 0.975-0.992), and 0.98 precision (95% CI 0.965-1.000), indicating a low false-positive rate on unseen samples. To ensure clinical trust, a dual Explainable AI (XAI) framework combining Grad-CAM and SHAP was implemented, providing localized visual heatmaps and global feature attribution. The proposed pipeline offers a statistically validated, generalizable, and interpretable computational framework, representing a rigorous foundation toward automated oral cancer screening support.

articles.title: Deep Learning-Based Scapular Morphology Assessment Pipeline for Glenoid Segmentation and Landmark Localization.
articles.abstract: Scapular morphology plays a critical role in the diagnosis and treatment of shoulder disorders. However, current assessment methods primarily rely on manual annotation of three-dimensional computed tomography (3D CT) scans by clinicians, which are time-consuming, labor-intensive, and prone to inter-observer variability. The objective of this study is to develop and validate a deep learning-based open-source pipeline for automated scapular morphology assessment, aiming to improve accuracy, reproducibility, and clinical efficiency. Descriptive Laboratory Study; Level of evidence, 2. We retrospectively collected 793 CT images of the shoulder from 774 patients (mean age, 60.00 ± 18.62 years). A 2D U-Net model performed high-resolution glenoid segmentation (native-resolution axial CT slices, no down-sampling), and a 3D nnUNet model was employed to localize five anatomical scapular landmarks: trigonum spinae (TS), angulus inferior (AI), processus coracoideus (PC), acromion (AC), and angulus acromialis (AA). Model performance was evaluated using the Dice coefficient and precision-recall metrics for glenoid segmentation and the Euclidean distance between the predicted and ground truth landmark position. This pipeline was designed as an automated open-source framework that can be readily integrated into clinical workflows or research environments through clinician-preferred user interface. The glenoid segmentation model achieved a 3D Dice coefficient of 98.46%, with a precision of 96.59% and a recall of 97.30%. The mean Euclidean localization error for the five scapular landmarks ranged from 1.0 to 2.0 mm. The entire assessment process took average 22.55 s per case. The proposed deep learning pipeline enables accurate, efficient, and reproducible assessment of scapular morphology. The proposed approach facilitates reliable and efficient diagnosis, offering a promising tool for clinical and research applications.

articles.title: A Hands-On Imaging Informatics Curriculum for Medical Students: Developing a Foundational Understanding of Healthcare Imaging Informatics.
articles.abstract: Imaging informatics is becoming more central to clinical practice with the expansion of artificial intelligence, telehealth, patient portals, and diagnostic imaging. Despite these technological advances, formal education in imaging informatics is typically not part of the traditional medical school curriculum. This paper describes the creation and implementation of a hands-on active learning module for medical students focused on foundational concepts in imaging informatics. The active learning module for second-year medical students was developed and led by faculty with expertise in imaging informatics. Students were instructed to view a brief prerecorded video prior to the session. During the in-person 50-min session, students were divided into groups of 6-10 and asked to take a photograph of a body part and send it to another team member. This process was repeated multiple times using a different image-sharing method and partner each time, followed by discussion of challenges encountered. Post-session evaluations yielded a mean rating of 4.33/5 for being conducive to learning and engaging the audience; opportunities to apply foundational concepts and activities that promoted problem solving each received mean ratings of 4.00/5. Qualitative feedback indicated that some students found the material new and applicable to clinical practice, while others desired more advanced content, clearer key takeaways, and additional information about physicians' roles in informatics. Qualitative feedback informed iterative modifications to the session. This educational session facilitated a rich discussion of core imaging informatics concepts including the importance of image standards, metadata to accompany images, workflow automation, and interoperability.

articles.title: CXR-CoRe: Two-Stage View- and Section-Aware Study-Level Chest X-ray Report Retrieval.
articles.abstract: Reliable linkage of chest X-ray examinations to corresponding reports is fundamental to large radiology archives. Yet heterogeneous view composition and similar image-report content across examinations, particularly longitudinal records, make exact content-based linkage difficult. Global vision-language representations support archive-wide search but can obscure view-specific and section-level correspondences, whereas exhaustive fine-grained interaction is computationally costly. We propose CXR-CoRe, a two-stage view- and section-aware framework. Stage 1 combines learned view embeddings with residual gated multi-view fusion, achieving 89.3% exact-pair coverage in its top-50 candidate set. Stage 2 reranks these candidates using patch-to-section correspondence and predicted clinical-label consistency, with same-subject inter-study negatives providing examination-specific supervision. On the full MIMIC-CXR test set of 3269 studies from 293 subjects, CXR-CoRe exceeded a controlled CXR-CLIP retraining by 3.8 and 5.0 percentage points in Recall@1 and Recall@5, respectively, and achieved higher Recall@10, mAP@5, and nDCG@5; the controlled baseline attained a lower MeanRank. Stage 2 improved all six metrics across three evaluation settings, with paired-bootstrap support at deeper cutoffs and in ranking quality. In GPU-resident online matching after shared feature extraction, candidate-limited matching was 16.3 times faster and used 93.6 times fewer estimated operations than full-archive one-layer cross-attention. These results establish coarse-to-fine retrieval as an effective strategy for exact study-level image-report linkage in large radiology archives.

articles.title: A Bayesian-Optimized Weighted Fuzzy Rank-Based Ensemble for Coronary Stenosis Detection in X-ray Angiography.
articles.abstract: X-ray coronary angiography is the gold standard for diagnosing coronary artery disease, a leading cause of global mortality. Existing artificial intelligence methods typically detect stenosis from individual frames or rely on manually selected key frames, despite angiography being inherently a video-based examination in which diagnostically relevant information appears only in a subset of frames. Moreover, conventional ensemble methods generally employ fixed classifier weights, limiting their ability to account for uncertainty and variations in classifier performance. To address these challenges, we propose a framework that combines automatic key-frame selection with a novel weighted fuzzy rank-based ensemble model for right coronary artery (RCA) stenosis detection. The framework employs a semi-supervised key-frame selection strategy using ResNet50 or ViT-B/16 as feature extractors together with a hybrid loss function for vessel segmentation. The selected key frames are then classified using a weighted fuzzy rank-based ensemble, which extends conventional fuzzy rank-based fusion by incorporating learnable classifier weights optimized through Bayesian optimization. Video-level predictions are obtained via majority voting over key-frame classifications, enabling clinically meaningful sequence-level assessment. The proposed method was evaluated on the publicly available AngioCAD dataset and further validated on the independent CADICA dataset. Experimental results demonstrate a video-level precision of 84.63%, F1-score of 80.44%, ROC-AUC of 70.06%, and PR-AUC of 81.83% on AngioCAD, while maintaining consistent performance on the external dataset, indicating good generalizability. The proposed framework may assist cardiologists in the rapid and reliable identification of coronary stenosis and support clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Practical applications of photon-counting CT in oncology: an organ-based pictorial review.
articles.abstract: Spectral computed tomography (CT) has become an important extension of contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) in oncologic imaging by providing material-specific information beyond conventional morphologic assessment. Dual-energy CT (DECT), implemented on energy-integrating detector CT (EID-CT) platforms, has demonstrated the value of low-keV virtual monoenergetic imaging (VMI), iodine mapping, and material decomposition for improving tumor conspicuity, delineating local extent, and supporting tissue characterization. However, broader clinical adoption of EID-CT-based DECT has been limited by increased low-keV image noise and workflow complexity. Photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT) addresses these limitations by offering improved energy resolution, reduced electronic noise, and routine acquisition of multi-energy data without dedicated dual-energy protocols. In particular, low-keV VMI around 40 keV can be generated with clinically acceptable noise, enabling consistent enhancement-based assessment in daily practice. Iodine-based reconstructions further complement morphologic evaluation by visualizing viable tumor enhancement and enabling quantitative analysis. This organ-based pictorial review summarizes practical applications of PCD-CT-based spectral imaging in oncology. Across organ systems, spectral CT may provide complementary problem-solving information by improving lesion detection, tumor extent delineation, and diagnostic confidence, particularly when conventional CT findings are equivocal, or MRI is unavailable, contraindicated, or limited. Emerging quantitative parameters, including electron density, effective atomic number, and advanced material decomposition, may further expand oncologic CT applications, although outcome-driven validation remains limited. Together, these features position PCD-CT as a practical spectral imaging platform for routine oncologic CT. KEY POINTS: Question How can PCD-CT address low-keV image noise and workflow barriers that have limited routine DECT-based spectral imaging in oncologic CT practice? Findings PCD-CT enables low-keV VMI and iodine-based reconstructions that may improve lesion conspicuity, tumor-extent assessment, and problem-solving across organ-specific oncologic workflows. Critical relevance statement This review clarifies practical, evidence-aware uses of PCD-CT spectral reconstructions in oncology, highlighting low-keV VMI as an adjunct, selective iodine-map problem-solving, and investigational quantitative parameters.

articles.title: The diagnostic value of high-resolution 3D T2-weighted MRI in preoperative evaluation and classification of Herlyn-Werner-Wunderlich syndrome: a prospective study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Herlyn-Werner-Wunderlich syndrome (HWWS) is a rare female reproductive tract malformation. Accurate preoperative diagnosis and classification are vital for surgical planning. This study aims to evaluate the diagnostic value of high-resolution three-dimensional (3D) T2-weighted MRI in the preoperative assessment and classification of HWWS. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The study prospectively enrolled 84 patients clinically diagnosed with HWWS between May 2020 and January 2025. Seventy patients underwent pelvic MRI examinations, including high-resolution 3D T2 sequences (1 mm slice thickness) and conventional T2 TSE sequences, supplemented by large-field-of-view (FOV) T2 coronal imaging for urinary system evaluation and full-spine X-ray examinations for skeletal assessment. Two experienced radiologists independently evaluated the imaging features in a blinded manner, focusing on uterine morphology, obstruction sites, presence of communications, and related anomalies and complications. Consistency analysis was performed between imaging findings and surgical results in 52 surgical patients. RESULTS: Uterine morphology included: didelphys (54/70, 77.1%), complete septate (14/70, 20%), and bicornuate uterus (2/70, 2.9%). Among 52 surgical patients, 31 (59.6%) had vaginal-level obstruction with 18 (34.6%) Type I, 11 (21.2%) Type II, and 2 (3.8%) Type III, and 21 (40.4%) had cervical-level obstruction (Type IV and mixed). 3D T2 sequences identified 7 (63.6%) vaginal septum fistulas, outperforming TSE sequences, which detected none (0%) (p = 0.005). Associated findings were ipsilateral renal agenesis (98.6%), ovarian endometriosis (22.9%), hematosalpinx (22.9%), and spinal abnormalities (scoliosis (25.7%), mild scoliosis (41.4%). CONCLUSION: High-resolution 3D T2 MRI is superior to conventional T2 TSE sequences in the preoperative evaluation of HWWS, especially for identifying communications and precisely locating obstruction sites. KEY POINTS: Question Accurate preoperative structural assessment and classification of HWWS are clinically essential, yet conventional MRI has limitations in identifying fine anatomical structures and small communications. Findings High-resolution 3D T2 MRI outperforms conventional T2 TSE in identifying vaginal and cervical communications and precisely localizing obstruction sites in preoperative evaluation of HWWS. Critical relevance statement This study supports routine inclusion of 3D sequences in HWWS imaging protocols. Combined with renal and spinal assessment, it provides a comprehensive preoperative evaluation that enhances surgical planning precision and optimizes patient management strategies.

articles.title: From Response Assessment to Biological Insight: PET/CT and Artificial Intelligence in Metastatic Breast Cancer.
MRI morphometric features and apparent diffusion coefficients predict muscle invasion in VI-RADS 3 bladder cancers.
articles.abstract: AIM: The present study investigated the clinical value of tumor MRI morphometric features and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) for predicting muscle invasion in bladder cancer of the vesical imaging reporting and data system (VI-RADS) 3. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Patients with VI-RADS 3 urothelial carcinoma of the bladder who had undergone radical cystectomy (RC) or partial cystectomy (PC) at our hospital between January 2018 and December 2024 were included. Two radiologists independently quantified tumor morphometrics and ADC parameters under expert supervision. RESULTS: A total of 96 patients were included, with 52 and 44 in the non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) group and muscle invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) group, respectively. Variables screened in the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression were the vertical diameter of the tumors, ADCmin of the tumors, ADCmean of the tumors, and ADCmean of the tumors' bases. Logistic multifactorial analysis showed that ADCmin of the tumors emerged as the sole independent predictor of MIBC (p<0.001) [OR=0.361 (95%CI: 0.21-0.62), p<0.001], with each 0.1 × 10-3 mm2/s increment reducing MIBC risk by 63.9 %. The area under the ROC curve for diagnosing MIBC and NMIBC with ADCmin of the tumor was 0.946 (95%CI: 0.904-0.988), achieving 88.6 % sensitivity and 90.4 % specificity at the cut off value of 0.854 × 10-3 mm2/s. CONCLUSIONS: The ADCmin of the tumor is the sole MRI-derived biomarker for predicting muscle invasion in VI-RADS 3 bladder cancer and is a valuable adjunct in the diagnosis.

articles.title: Shear Wave Elastography of the Tibial Nerve and Lower Limb Nerve-Muscle-Tendon Complex in Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy: Elastic Alterations and Clinical Implications.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate the associations among diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN), diabetic tendinopathy, and diabetic myopathy and their respective influencing factors using shear wave elastography (SWE). METHODS: This study enrolled 65 diabetic patients (22 with DPN [PN-DM group], 43 without DPN [NPN-DM group]) and 35 healthy controls. Their general clinical data and laboratory indicators were collected. High-resolution ultrasound and SWE evaluated the morphology and elasticity of the tibial nerve (TN), Achilles tendon (AT), and medial head of gastrocnemius (MG). Parameters were compared among 3 groups. RESULTS: Diabetic patients exhibited larger cross-sectional area (CSA) and transverse diameter (TD) of the TN than controls (all p < .05). Longitudinal TN shear wave velocity (SWV) progressively increased from controls to NPN-DM to PN-DM groups. The right TN Emax (cutoff: 3.87 m/s) demonstrated the highest diagnostic accuracy for DPN, with 90.9% sensitivity and 61.8% specificity. Diabetic patients displayed significantly reduced cross-sectional AT SWV, as well as lower absolute difference in pennation angle and SWV of the MG than controls (p < .01). The AT's SWV and MG's ΔSWV correlated positively (p < .001), but neither correlated with TN's SWV. HbA1c was independently associated with all 3 structures' elasticity (p < .05). CONCLUSIONS: TN's SWV increased significantly from the control to NPN-DM, and further to the PN-DM group. AT and MG's elasticity decreased significantly in diabetic patients with a positive correlation, but neither correlated with TN's elasticity. HbA1c was the solely independent risk factor common to the TN, AT, and MG elasticity.
